title: Best AI Tools for Windchill Users in 2027
summary: Nov 26, 2026 | Compare the best AI tools for Windchill, from design review and engineering search to semantic PLM search and cross-system knowledge.
body_markdown:
**The best AI tools for Windchill users include CoLab for AI and human design review, PTC’s native tools for document search and part rationalization, and third-party options from Leo AI, Fishbowl Solutions, Sinequa, and Savaco.**


In this guide, we compare what’s available natively in Windchill PLM with third-party options, covering each tool’s capabilities, integration, and suitability for mechanical engineering teams. We also explain where the products overlap and which differences matter when choosing between them.


*Vendor note. This guide is published by CoLab. We build software for AI and human design review and integrate with Windchill, so we are active participants in this market. Our comparison focuses on the engineering tasks each tool supports and how it connects to Windchill.*

## **Native AI tools in Windchill**


PTC offers two native capabilities worth considering before adding another platform. However, their availability depends on your Windchill release, configuration, and licensing.


**Windchill AI Assistant** adds a natural language chat interface through PTC’s AI plugin. Engineers can ask questions about indexed Windchill documents, retrieve requirements, or summarize technical documentation, then open the cited sources to verify the response. Depending on configuration, it can also answer questions using PTC help and support content.


Those answers come from the text in supported documents attached to parts, CAD records, and change records. For example, the assistant can retrieve a requirement from a drawing PDF’s selectable notes, but it cannot inspect the geometry shown in that drawing or analyze images. Results remain subject to the user’s existing access permissions.


**AI Parts Rationalization** uses shape similarity to identify potential duplicate parts. PTC generates the comparison from lightweight 3D representations called PVZ files. Because the model does not account for material, scale, or part attributes, engineers still need to compare dimensions and specifications before deciding that an existing part can replace a proposed one.


### **When to choose PTC’s native AI**


Choose Windchill AI Assistant when your priority is finding answers in technical documentation already stored in Windchill. Choose AI Parts Rationalization when you want to identify candidates for part reuse or consolidation within your existing parts library. Neither capability replaces an engineering assessment of a drawing, a component’s manufacturability, or its suitability for a particular assembly.


Our[AI for PLM comparison](https://www.colabsoftware.com/post/best-ai-for-plm?utm_source=chatgpt.com) covers how other product lifecycle management platforms approach AI. Here, the focus is on what you can add to an existing Windchill environment.


## **Best third-party AI tools for Windchill users**


### **1. CoLab for AI design review and engineering decisions**


CoLab is the strongest fit in this comparison for manufacturers that need AI checks to feed directly into design reviews with manufacturing, quality, and suppliers.


[AutoReview](https://www.colabsoftware.com/product/autoreview?utm_source=chatgpt.com) , CoLab’s AI peer checker, reviews drawings for dimensional errors and standards violations, and runs geometric manufacturability checks on 3D models. When a finding needs investigation, engineers can use[Operator](https://www.colabsoftware.com/operator?utm_source=chatgpt.com) to retrieve applicable standards and previous design feedback available in CoLab.


Engineers can then discuss those findings with reviewers, assign changes, and[compare revised designs against the original feedback](https://www.colabsoftware.com/use-case/design-review-cad?utm_source=chatgpt.com) . The discussion preserves why each change was made, making that reasoning available for future decisions.[Schaeffler used CoLab alongside Windchill to centralize design discussions and follow-up actions](https://www.colabsoftware.com/case-studies/schaeffler?utm_source=chatgpt.com) , reporting 2x faster design cycles with less review administration.


#### **How CoLab works with Windchill**


The review starts with **Share with CoLab** , an action added to Windchill when an administrator installs the integration. Engineers select an assembly and its associated models, drawings, and documents, then send them into a CoLab workspace.


Manufacturing engineers and suppliers can then inspect the designs and comment on geometry in a browser without Windchill access. CoLab workspace permissions govern their access, while engineers can see review status back in Windchill. Our[integration walkthrough](https://www.colabsoftware.com/post/windchill-for-engineering-design-review?utm_source=chatgpt.com) explains the sharing and permission controls.


Teams using Creo can also start from **Share & Review** in the CAD ribbon, preserving revision and iteration metadata for files opened through Windchill. Our[Creo tools comparison](https://www.colabsoftware.com/post/best-ai-tools-for-creo?utm_source=chatgpt.com) covers that route.


#### **When to choose CoLab**


Choose CoLab when you need automated checks and manufacturing or supplier input on Windchill-managed designs, especially when reviewers use different CAD or PLM systems.


[CoLab’s other integrations](https://www.colabsoftware.com/product/integrations) include NX, SOLIDWORKS, Teamcenter, SOLIDWORKS PDM, and 3DEXPERIENCE. For example, your team can share an assembly from Windchill while a supplier shares tooling from NX. Both teams can review those designs together in CoLab without accessing each other’s CAD or PLM systems.


### **2. Leo AI for part reuse and design inspection**


Leo’s Windchill connection supports part search, while its Inspector feature checks designs against engineering criteria and supplied standards.


#### **How Leo works with Windchill**


After a team selects which Windchill folders or projects Leo can access, Leo reads and indexes the latest files without checking them in or out. Engineers can also connect the model open in CAD through a separate add-in, with integration depth depending on the CAD application.


#### **When to choose Leo**


Consider Leo for finding reusable parts in Windchill and checking CAD models. If manufacturing teams or suppliers also need to review those designs, look for a tool that lets them view models, discuss changes, and track design issues without needing Windchill access.


### **3. Fishbowl Solutions for Windchill search and related product information**


Fishbowl Solutions offers Generative AI for Windchill, with packages for product information search and analysis of relationships among parts, assemblies, and suppliers.


#### **How Fishbowl works with Windchill**


The base package combines Fishbowl SearchIndex with Oracle Cloud Infrastructure to provide natural language search inside Windchill, returning answers with links to source records. If engineers also need information from other repositories, a higher tier connects up to three additional sources. A separate Neo4j graph add-on extends the offering to BOM and supplier relationship analysis.


#### **When to choose Fishbowl**


Fishbowl is a fit when engineers lose time locating drawings, BOMs, or change records in Windchill. However, its published packages do not specify automated GD&T or geometric DFM checks, so teams seeking those capabilities would still need a design checking solution.


### **4. Sinequa for engineering search across enterprise systems**


Sinequa is the enterprise search product within Argonos’s broader enterprise AI platform.


For a mechanical engineer investigating a recurring component failure, the specification may be in Windchill while test reports and quality records sit elsewhere. Sinequa can search those connected sources using descriptive queries or exact terms such as part numbers.


#### **How Sinequa works with Windchill**


Your IT team configures the Windchill connector and other repositories to be indexed. Engineers can then search across them and inspect the supporting records, with access checked against source-system permissions.


Because those answers rely on an index, the configured update schedule determines when revised Windchill documents become searchable.


#### **When to choose Sinequa**


Choose Sinequa when engineers need information from Windchill and several other systems, and your IT team can support the connections and indexing. It helps engineers assemble the information needed for an investigation; drawing checks and supplier reviews require additional capabilities.


### **5. Savaco PLM Buddy for Windchill queries and record creation**


Savaco is an engineering and IT services provider. Its PLM Buddy product connects Microsoft Copilot to Windchill so engineers can query an assembly’s bill of materials, or BOM, and retrieve part details through chat. It also supports creating or updating problem reports and creating change notices.


#### **How Savaco works with Windchill**


Savaco deploys a Model Context Protocol, or MCP, server in your organization’s Azure environment to connect Copilot with selected Windchill APIs. When an engineer requests a BOM or asks Copilot to create a change notice, that service calls the relevant Windchill function using the engineer’s existing access rights.


#### **When to choose Savaco PLM Buddy**


Choose PLM Buddy when your team already uses Microsoft Copilot and wants to retrieve Windchill data or create problem reports and change notices through chat. The available actions are limited to the Windchill functions exposed through the connector, so expanding beyond them requires further implementation. This can simplify the administration around an engineering change, while the design analysis and review behind that change remain separate.


## **How to choose an AI tool for Windchill**


Before a vendor demo, choose an assembly your team has already reviewed and can share. Consider including its drawing, an earlier revision, and the company guideline(s) behind a known issue. Your engineers can then judge the software against a design they understand, including the concerns it should find and the changes that were actually required.


For **drawing and CAD review** , ask the vendor to run its checks on the earlier revision. Does it catch the issue your team found, identify the relevant feature or callout, and explain which guideline applies? Then ask how a manufacturing engineer would add feedback, how the designer would return the revised file, and how the reviewer would compare that file with the original concern. Our[engineering drawings guide](https://www.colabsoftware.com/guides/ai-for-engineering-drawings?utm_source=chatgpt.com) explains the capabilities to look for in automated checks.


For **search and part reuse** , give the vendor a question your team recently had to answer, such as which existing housing meets a particular material and dimensional requirement. Ask it to open the supporting drawing and specification, identify their revisions, and show which sources were searched. If the answer depends on a past design decision, the software needs access to its recorded explanation. Our article on[capturing design intent](https://www.colabsoftware.com/post/building-an-engineering-knowledge-base-for-ai-agents-can-we-capture-design-intent?utm_source=chatgpt.com) explains how to preserve that reasoning during review.


Finally, involve your Windchill administrator in the integration discussion. For a search index, ask the vendor when a newly released drawing replaces the previous version in search results. For a review platform, ask how the revised file reaches the reviewers and which permissions govern their access. For agentic AI that creates or modifies Windchill records, have the vendor walk through a specific action and identify exactly where an engineer reviews and authorizes it.


## **Bring Windchill-managed designs into AI and human review**


When a manufacturing concern is resolved during design review, the resulting CAD revision becomes part of the product record. The reasoning behind it can also help another engineer avoid repeating the problem, provided the team captures that reasoning and can retrieve it when needed.

Windchill continues to manage controlled product data and formal release processes.
